clue.text: Get on this well, as the arsonist would seem to do

definitions.meaning: to get on extremely well with someone is to get on in this fashion, an idiom for rapid friendship

definitions.text: as the arsonist would seem to do
definitions.meaning: read literally, a fire-raiser would be fond of a building in flames

explanation.surface: A remark that getting along well is how an arsonist behaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two people hitting it off quickly and warmly; taken literally it describes enjoying a burning building.

clue.text: A record we hear, by this composer

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the word is taken as it is spoken, not written

parts.note: a list is a written record of items

explanation.surface: Someone reports hearing a record made by a particular composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' marks a sound-alike: LIST, a record, said aloud gives the Hungarian composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Has a bird and perseveres

parts.note: to have something, such as a pet, is to keep it
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone owns a pet bird and refuses to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read KEEPS A TIT, which respaced gives the phrase for carrying on doggedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep at something is to persist with effort despite difficulty.

clue.text: Matter, but half the 'alphabet needed to describe it

definitions.meaning: physical stuff is made of tiny particles of this kind
the letters from A as far as M make up the first half of the 26-letter alphabet

explanation.surface: A comment that you need half the alphabet to describe matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe is a printing blemish. Respaced, the answer reads A TO M, the first thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter is built from these smallest units of a chemical element.

clue.text: Card game for a single player?

definitions.meaning: a children's card game in which players avoid being left holding the odd queen
an unmarried woman of mature years, here imagined as someone playing alone

explanation.surface: A question about which card game suits someone playing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the simple matching card game is also an old term for a woman who never married.

clue.text: Conceal dam below the point

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting below another comes after it

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: An instruction to hide a dam beneath a certain point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' suggests a water barrier, but it is a breeder's word for a mother animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover it up so it cannot be seen or expressed, to suppress it.

clue.text: A man out to reassemble a mechanical device

indicators.note: putting the parts together again in a different arrangement signals that the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A man is sent out to put a machine back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reassemble' turns A MAN OUT TO, nine letters, into the answer; the second 'to' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine, often a figure that moves by clockwork.

clue.text: Unsuitable paint explodes

indicators.note: something that explodes is blown apart, so the letters of the word paint are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Unsuitable paint blows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means not fitting or appropriate for the situation.

clue.text: Given possible cause of death, inter hastily in elevated site

indicators.note: one group of letters is placed inside another
in a down clue, raising a word up makes it read from bottom to top, so site runs backwards
doing a burial hastily suggests a jumbled, careless rearrangement of the word inter

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to bury a body quickly on high ground, given the cause of death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is a link word. The burial surface hides the mechanics: 'hastily' scrambles the second word into NTERI, 'elevated' reads the last word upwards as ETIS, and 'in' sets one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteritis, inflammation of the intestine, can be fatal, especially in the young or animals.

clue.text: Editor's handed out dope

indicators.note: things handed out are distributed and dispersed, so the letters are spread and rearranged

parts.note: the word with its possessive s supplies all eight letters as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is supplying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handed out' rearranges the letters EDITORS, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for performance-enhancing drugs given illicitly to athletes or animals, steroids being a classic example.

clue.text: Reject a call for strike in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a person rejected by society, used as a noun

definitions.text: a call for strike in the theatre
definitions.meaning: the cry 'Out!' addressed to the actors, as a union leader calls workers out on strike

explanation.surface: A theatrical call for the actors to walk out, or a rejected person.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a pariah, someone society has driven away; split, it is the cry summoning the players out.

clue.text: River trial

definitions.meaning: a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout fishing
an examination of ability or quality

explanation.definitionFit: The Hampshire trout river shares its name with an examination of skill or performance.

clue.text: Measuring rotation of comet and earth

definitions.text: Measuring rotation of comet and earth

indicators.note: turning the two words round signals that their letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An astronomer measures how a comet and the Earth spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotation of' mixes the ten letters of COMET and EARTH; the whole clue also describes what the instrument does.
explanation.definitionFit: This dial or gauge shows how fast a shaft or engine is revolving, in turns per minute.

clue.text: Took turns to read out gripping Times leader

indicators.note: the anagram holds the other letter tightly inside it
letters put out of place are rearranged
a leader comes first, so the opening letter of Times is taken

explanation.surface: Someone takes turns reading aloud an editorial grip of The Times leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TO READ into ROATED; 'gripping' puts T, the 'leader' of Times, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to take turns in a set order, as staff do with shifts.

clue.text: Not allowed to marry when in hospital

definitions.text: Not allowed to marry when in hospital

parts.words: Not allowed to marry when in hospital
parts.note: one official title covers both a civil marriage officiant and a senior hospital doctor, who has no power to wed couples

explanation.surface: Someone is forbidden to wed while a patient in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a patient barred from marrying; really the same job title in a hospital means a doctor, not the register-office official.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names both the officer who conducts civil weddings and a hospital doctor ranking below consultant.

clue.text: Athletic kit for linesman?

parts.note: a runner's warm-up outfit, imagined as clothing suited to someone who maintains railway lines

explanation.surface: A question about what sportswear a linesman should wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linesman' suggests a football official; here it is someone who works on the railway, whose track gives the outfit its name.
explanation.definitionFit: This loose jacket-and-trousers outfit is worn by athletes for training or warming up.

clue.text: Troops parley, then withdraw

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army
to treat is to negotiate or discuss terms with an enemy

explanation.surface: Soldiers negotiate, then pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to fall back or move away, as an army does after losing ground.

clue.text: Is this ell a must?

parts.note: the clue toys with letter names like ess, en and ell, which the answer sounds partly built from, while asking if something is indispensable

explanation.surface: A question whether a particular L-shaped extension is truly needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer said slowly runs through letter names (ess, en, ... ell), which is the joke behind 'ell'; 'a must' gives the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indispensable, which cannot be done without, is a requirement or necessity.

clue.text: Spotted in a narrow passage beside the gal lory

indicators.note: one piece is set right next to the other

parts.note: a gut is a narrow channel or strait
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Something was seen in a narrow corridor next to the art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as 'seen', but it means covered with spots, a botanical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Guttate describes something marked with drop-like spots, used in botany and medicine.

clue.text: No longer, model army unit-too radical

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what it was
the Model T was Ford's famous early car
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A former model reports that an army unit has become too radical.
explanation.walkthrough: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme views go well beyond moderation, as fanatical or immoderate positions do.

clue.text: Book production?

definitions.meaning: the first book of the Bible
the coming into being of something, its origin or creation

explanation.surface: A question about how a book comes to be made.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening book of the Bible tells of the creation, and the word also means the origin of anything.

clue.text: Gay heroine has festive meal

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration or occasion
tea is a light afternoon or early evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: A cheerful heroine sits down to a celebratory meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is John Gay, who wrote the libretto of Handel's Acis and Galatea; the surface wants the adjective 'merry'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea-nymph of Gay's libretto for Handel's opera is the beloved of the shepherd Acis.

clue.text: Fills up cashbox without turning a hair

parts.note: to stock a shop is to fill its shelves
a till is the drawer holding a shop's money

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper calmly loads the cash register.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely motionless means not moving a muscle, not so much as a hair stirring.

clue.text: Stonecrop, yellow, crest of peak

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Stonecrop, yellow, crest of peak (5)': OR (yellow) plus P (crest of peak) leaves IN unaccounted for; no clue word supplies it, so the clue appears cut short.

clue.text: Knob for tipping back the bed

indicators.note: tipping a thing backwards turns it over, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a bunk is a narrow bed, often one of a stacked pair

explanation.surface: A knob used to tilt the bed backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: KNUB is a dialect word for a small knob or lump.
explanation.definitionFit: This dialect word means a small lump or protuberance.

clue.text: He can't be persuaded to move in any little matter

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bit is a small amount of anything
to go is to move

explanation.surface: Someone who won't budge on even the smallest point.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stops at 'persuaded'; 'to move' starts the wordplay, and 'in' places the moving word inside the small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot holds prejudiced opinions and refuses to consider other views.

clue.text: Dash from hotel annexe

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words hotel annexe

explanation.surface: Someone rushes out of a hotel's annexe.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash here means style and flair, energetic confidence.

clue.text: Put out, receiving unexpected hug? It's sheer bliss!

indicators.note: the outer piece wraps around the inner as arms embrace someone

parts.note: something rare is uncommon and so comes unexpectedly

indicators.note: letters put out of place are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at a surprise embrace finds it wonderful after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'annoyed', but 'out' scrambles the first word into PTU, and 'hug' has the word for unexpected wrapped around it; 'receiving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is a state of intense joy or ecstasy.

clue.text: Listing in the lists?

definitions.meaning: leaning to one side, as a ship does
the lists were the enclosed field where knights jousted

explanation.surface: A question about listing items within lists.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both leaning over and charging with a lance in a joust.

clue.text: Travels down a lane and is attacked by strikers

definitions.text: Travels down a lane and is attacked by strikers

parts.words: Travels down a lane and is attacked by strikers
parts.note: an old punishment in which the victim passed between two rows of men who beat him as he went

explanation.surface: Someone walking down a lane is set upon by people on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikers' suggests workers in a dispute; here they are simply people hitting the victim.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a military punishment of passing between lines of men wielding sticks, and now means facing criticism.
